settings.heading: We made coffee for the places we'd rather be.

settings.text: We buy direct from a handful of farms we visit each year. Smaller lots, fairer prices, and a list of names instead of a co-op number.
The coffee gets roasted in small batches in Brooklyn, ground the same week, and sealed into a compostable filter. Then it leaves the warehouse and shows up at your door.

settings.title: Tear.
settings.body: Open the notch and tear straight across. No scissors, no mess.

settings.title: Soak.
settings.body: Hang the tab over the rim of your mug and pour hot water through the filter until it's fully submerged.

settings.title: Wait.
settings.body: Five minutes. Don't check your phone. We wrote a timer in case you need one.

settings.title: Lift.
settings.body: Lift the filter out, give it one gentle press against the mug, and sip.

settings.quote: "You can drink coffee with two bars of signal, or no bars at all. The coffee doesn't care. Maybe you don't either."

settings.heading:
Compostable.
Not just recyclable.
settings.tag: 100% Plant-based filter · OK for your backyard compost
settings.body: The filter is plant fiber and corn starch. The wrapper is uncoated kraft. The box is the box. Bury the whole thing in the garden and it'll be soil by spring.
